title: Up and Down in the prompt skip over wrapped rows
body:
The prompt box draws its text in rows. `wrap_rows` in `ui.rs` breaks the text at word breaks to the box's width, and every `\n` starts a new row. The cursor keys see only the `\n` lines. Up and Down in `App`'s prompt key handling call `prompt::line_above` and `prompt::line_below`. Both find the neighbouring line by searching for `\n` and keep the display column.

When a line wraps, its rows are one line to these functions. In a single paragraph that wraps to three rows, Up and Down do nothing, because no line lies above or below it. With the cursor on the first row of a wrapped paragraph, Down jumps past the paragraph's remaining rows to the next `\n` line.

## Proposal

Up and Down move by drawn row. They keep the display column, as they do now. To find the rows, the movement code needs the width `wrap_rows` was given. `App` would keep the prompt's width from the last draw, the way it keeps `page` for Page Up and Page Down.

Ctrl-A and Ctrl-E stay on the `\n` line. coax takes them from readline and Emacs, and both move by logical line.
close_reason: Done in 14b6bdf. `prompt::row_above` and `prompt::row_below` move by the rows `prompt::wrap_rows` draws, at the width `App::prompt_width` keeps from the last draw. Ctrl-A and Ctrl-E still move by `\n` line.
